headline: Simple Urine Test Detects Bladder Cancer With 92% Accuracy
meta_description: A new genetic urine test detected bladder cancer in 71 of 77 patients in a UK study, offering a non-invasive alternative to costly cystoscopy procedures.
summary_short: A groundbreaking UK study shows a simple urine test successfully identified bladder cancer in 92% of cases, potentially transforming how the disease is screened.
body:
A British observational study has validated a remarkably simple yet sophisticated approach to bladder cancer detection: a genetic urine test that correctly identified cancer in 71 of 77 patients who developed the disease. The test, called GALEAS Bladder, analyzes a routine urine sample for traces of 23 genes associated with bladder cancer, achieving a negative predictive value greater than 99%—meaning it is exceptionally reliable at ruling out disease. The study, published in European Urology Oncology and conducted between 2024 and 2025 across 964 referred patients, suggests this innovation could substantially reduce the burden on healthcare systems while improving patient experience.

The current standard for bladder cancer diagnosis—flexible cystoscopy combined with imaging and tissue analysis—is expensive, invasive, and time-consuming. By contrast, GALEAS requires only what patients can provide effortlessly: a urine sample, potentially even one collected for unrelated reasons. This matters because bladder cancer affects roughly 550,000 people globally each year, yet a bewildering gap exists in current screening: although blood in urine appears in over 90% of diagnosed cases, only 8–19% of patients referred for testing actually receive a positive diagnosis. At Dorset County Hospital Foundation Trust in the UK, where the evaluation took place, lead nurse consultant Andy Goffe noted that 100% of patients agreed to participate, finding the non-invasive nature deeply appealing.

The study identified all 17 muscle-invasive cancers and 35 of 36 advanced-stage cases, though the test did produce 61 false positives and miss 6 cancers, four at very early stages. Researchers concluded that as a triage tool—a first-pass screening device—GALEAS demonstrated considerable reliability and accuracy. Should it be adopted widely, the test could meaningfully reduce waiting times for urgent cystoscopies and spare thousands from unnecessary invasive procedures each year.
quick_facts: GALEAS Bladder detected cancer in 71 of 77 cases in UK study
Negative predictive value greater than 99% accuracy
100% patient participation rate at Dorset County Hospital
Analyzes urine for traces of 23 cancer-associated genes
